claims.text: The target material is bulk single-crystal HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
A machine-learning-enhanced Boltzmann transport solver can combine DFT phonon properties with explicit alloy mass-disorder and oxygen-defect scattering rates.
Explicit treatment of alloy disorder and oxygen point defects provides a better representation of phonon scattering than virtual-crystal and perfect-crystal approximations.
Training on DFT-computed scattering rates enables the ML model to capture non-perturbative mass- and defect-scattering contributions to phonon lifetimes.
Capturing these scattering contributions improves predictions of thermal resistivity at low and high temperatures.
For HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen, the proposed solver will reduce conductivity-prediction mean absolute error by at least 20% relative to analytical models.
The at-least-20% error reduction will occur separately in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Klemens-type models and classical phonon-gas models are the relevant analytical baselines.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk, single-crystal HfNbTaTiZr with no more than 1 wt.% oxygen over 0–1200 K.
The approach has not been tested on polycrystals or materials containing other defect types.
Low-temperature alloy scattering is likely to be captured well by the proposed model.
High-temperature anharmonicity may degrade the model's performance.
Oxygen concentrations above 1 wt.% may degrade the model's performance.
Thermal conductivity should be measured from 0–200 K and 300–1200 K on a bulk HfNbTaTiZr single crystal containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Prediction MAE should be computed for both the ML-augmented solver and the analytical baselines.
Failure to achieve at least 20% lower MAE than the analytical baseline in either temperature regime falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparator is characterized as assuming a defect-free or perfect crystal, but the listed Klemens mass-disorder model explicitly represents mass-disorder scattering. The hypothesis therefore conflates perfect-crystal models with a disorder-aware analytical baseline.
